title: Sliding Windows in Practice
excerpt: Sliding window attention limits each token to a fixed span of earlier tokens, which keeps memory flat as sequences grow. The idea is old, but it only became popular once long contexts did.

Rolling buffers keep the cache at the window size, so a sequence ten times longer than the window costs no more memory than one that just fits. That property matters more than raw speed for most deployments.
Taken together, these choices make long inputs cheap without changing the model's quality on short ones, which is the trade most teams want when they first reach for a longer context.

The buffer is indexed modulo the window size, so old entries are overwritten in place.
